label: HEALING

cover.headline: Moving on *when you still see him*
cover.sub: Shared friends, work, or the same gym.

points.heading: Plan for the moments
points.body: Knowing you might see him helps you feel less caught off guard.
points.panel: Decide in advance how you’ll greet him: short and polite.

points.heading: Keep it simple and kind
points.body: You don’t owe a long conversation.
points.panel: “Hi, hope you’re well.” Then move on.

points.heading: Bring a buffer
points.body: A friend nearby makes shared spaces easier.
points.panel: “Will you come with me to the party? He might be there.”

points.heading: Limit the scrolling
points.body: Seeing him online keeps the wound open.
points.panel: Mute his posts for now. You can decide later.

points.heading: Let it get easier slowly
points.body: The first few times are hardest. It does fade.
points.panel: “That was hard, and I handled it.”

close.save: Save this for the next encounter.

caption:
Moving on is hard enough. It’s even harder when you still see him at work, with friends, or around town.

You can’t always avoid the moments, but you can prepare for them. These five steps help you stay steady and protect your healing, even when he’s in the room.
